guidance.heading: Choose by the job
guidance.body: Running wire rope: 202 Standard, or 202 White where a dark grease would stain paintwork. New wires and cold climates: 101 oil first, with 202 on top — the two mix. Threads and rails that must not be painted: 202 Aluminium grease paint. Parts going into storage: 103 drying oil.

standards.heading: Built for wires at sea

items.q: Grease or oil on a wire rope?
items.a: Oil (Ferryl 101) penetrates the core best and stays workable in the cold; grease (Ferryl 202) holds on the outside and lubricates. On new wires, use the oil first and the grease on top.

items.q: Should a rusty wire be cleaned first?
items.a: Yes. Old grease, rust and moisture left in the rope are sealed in under a new coat and the wire rusts from within. Clean it, then re-grease.

products.title: Ferryl 202 Standard Anticorrosive Wire Rope Grease
products.descriptionShort: Ferryl 202 Standard is a marine wire rope grease for mooring, crane, ramp and winch wires: it works into the core, holds on in heavy weather and does not drip in tropical heat. 25 kg drum or 900 g tin.
products.descriptionLong:
Ferryl 202 Standard is the grease Ferryl built its name on: a wire rope grease made for wires that work on open deck, in salt spray and in climates that swing from freezing to tropical. It protects a steel wire rope against rust and keeps the strands lubricated, so the rope wears less as it runs over sheaves and onto winch drums.

Why it stays on the wire

  • It penetrates into the core of the rope, so the inner strands are protected as well as the outside.
  • Rubberised binders make it cling to the wire, so it is not thrown off when the rope runs or washed off in a storm.
  • A semi-drying film forms on the surface. It keeps moisture out and stays flexible, so it does not crack as the rope bends.
  • A high melting point stops it dripping onto decks, cargo or the sea in hot weather, and it stays workable below freezing.
  • Chemically active rust inhibitors protect the steel where the film is thin.

Where it is used

Mooring wires and backsprings, ship and offshore crane wires, ro-ro ramp wires, lifeboat falls, derricks and hoists — and, beyond wire rope, open gears, winches, shackles, lashings, hatch-cover wheels, tank-cover screws, valves, bearings, screws and bolts.

How to apply it

Apply by brush or glove, or pump it through the Ferryl Wire Rope Lubricator, which presses the grease into the core in one pass. On a new wire, or where full core penetration matters, Ferryl recommends a first coat of Ferryl 101 Anticorrosive Oil with 202 Standard on top. The two are fully compatible and can be mixed to soften the grease for cold-weather application. On a used or rusty wire, clean off old grease, rust and moisture first, or they are sealed in under the new coat.

Packs

25 kg metal drum, or a 900 g tin for small jobs.

products.title: Ferryl 202 White Anticorrosive Wire Rope Grease
products.descriptionShort: Ferryl 202 White is a white marine wire rope grease for lifeboat falls, davit wires, ro-ro ramp wires and mooring wires where a dark grease would stain white paintwork. 30 kg drum.
products.descriptionLong:
Ferryl 202 White does the same job as Ferryl 202 Standard — rust protection and lubrication for wire rope at sea — in a white grease. It is the choice where appearance matters: lifeboat and tender falls on cruise ships and ferries, ramp wires on car carriers and ro-ro vessels, and any wire that runs over white paintwork, vehicles or passengers.

How it performs

  • Rubberised binders hold it on the wire, so it is not flung off when tenders are lowered or the ramp is worked.
  • A semi-drying film keeps seawater out of the rope and stays flexible as it bends.
  • A high melting point stops it dripping in tropical heat; it remains workable below freezing.
  • It penetrates into the core, and chemically active rust inhibitors protect the steel.
  • Better adhesion means it lasts longer on the wire, so re-greasing is needed less often.

Where it is used

Lifeboat falls and davit wires, ramp wires on PCC, PCTC and ro-ro vessels, steel mooring wires as an alternative to 202 Standard, and the same deck hardware: winches, shackles, hatch-cover wheels, open gears, lashings, valves and bearings.

How to apply it

By brush or glove, or through the Ferryl Wire Rope Lubricator. Clean used or rusty wires before you apply it.

Pack

30 kg metal drum.

products.title: Ferryl 202 Aluminium Anticorrosive Grease (Grease Paint)
products.descriptionShort: Ferryl 202 Aluminium is an aluminium-pigmented "grease paint" for container lashings, turnbuckles, hatch-cover and crane rails: paint-like cover that never dries hard, −30 °C to +70 °C. 30 kg drum.
products.descriptionLong:
Ferryl 202 Aluminium sits between a grease and a paint. It goes on in a thin, paint-like coat, but it never dries hard, so it does not crack or peel where steel moves, flexes or carries a rolling load. Ferryl calls it a grease paint. The aluminium in it gives anti-seize protection on threads and an aluminium-grey colour that blends in on deck hardware.

Where it earns its place

  • Container lashings and turnbuckles. A thicker grease is wiped off the thread as it turns, and what is left washes away. A thin coat of 202 Aluminium stays on, protects the thread and keeps it easy to open and close.
  • Hatch-cover and gantry-crane rails. Paint is scraped off by the wheels, and general-purpose grease is squeezed out under load. 202 Aluminium stays flexible under the wheel and resists seawater.
  • Hatch-cover wheels, gear wheels, shackles, tank-cover screws, external hot spindles, engine-room fasteners, screws and bolts.

How it performs

  • Ferryl rates it for −30 °C to +70 °C on open deck, in salt water and in sunlight.
  • It does not drip in tropical heat and does not go brittle below freezing.
  • Strong adhesion and seawater resistance; it is not easily washed off.
  • Chemically active rust inhibitors.

How to apply it

By brush, glove or grease gun. A thin layer is enough.

Pack

30 kg metal drum.

products.title: Ferryl 101 Anticorrosive Wire Rope Oil
products.descriptionShort: Ferryl 101 is a penetrating anticorrosive oil for wire rope: it soaks into the core, leaves a semi-drying film and stays easy to apply well below freezing. Use alone or under Ferryl 202 grease. 25 L drum.
products.descriptionLong:
Ferryl 101 is the oil partner to Ferryl 202 Standard grease. Because it is liquid it runs right through a wire rope to the core, carrying Ferryl's rust inhibitors with it, then sets into a semi-drying film that keeps moisture out without cracking.

When to use it

  • As a first coat on new wires, or wherever full penetration matters, with 202 Standard applied on top for external protection and lubrication.
  • In cold climates. Greases stiffen as the temperature drops and can become too hard to apply. Ferryl 101 stays easy to work well below freezing and can be used alone on vessels greasing wires in the cold.
  • To soften 202 Standard. The two products are fully compatible; mixing them gives a softer consistency for cold-weather work or a particular application method.

How it performs

  • Superior penetration into the wire core.
  • Wide temperature range, including well below freezing.
  • Chemically active rust inhibitors.
  • Strong adhesion to the wire.
  • Semi-drying, flexible film that keeps moisture out.
  • Lubricates against wear for easy running of rigging.

Where it is used

Mooring wires and backsprings, crane and ramp wires, lifeboat falls, hoists and derricks, and on winches, shackles, valves, bearings, lashings, screws and bolts.

How to apply it

By brush or glove, or through the Ferryl Wire Rope Lubricator.

Pack

25 litre metal drum.

products.title: Ferryl 103 Anticorrosive Drying Oil
products.descriptionShort: Ferryl 103 is a rust-preventive drying oil that sets to a tough, dry, waxy film for spare parts, shafts, propellers, tools and tanks in storage — and comes off with a degreaser when the part is needed. 25 L drum.
products.descriptionLong:
Spare parts usually arrive with a thin transport oil that is not meant to survive months in a humid, salty store room or on an open deck. Ferryl 103 replaces it with real long-term protection: an oil that dries to a tough, dry, waxy film carrying Ferryl's rust inhibitors, sealing the metal off from salt, air and water.

How it works

  • Dries completely to a dry, tough coat — parts can be handled and stacked.
  • The coat can be built up thinner or thicker to suit how long the part will be stored and where.
  • Strong adhesion and chemically active rust inhibitors for long-term protection.
  • A high melting point and good low-temperature behaviour for storage in hot or freezing conditions.
  • Comes off easily with a degreaser, so the part goes back into service in its original condition.

Ferryl states that parts coated with 103 can be stored for several years without corrosion underneath.

Where it is used

Spare parts and machine parts, spare propellers, shafts and axles, engines and machinery laid up, pipes, tanks and void spaces, chain cable, tools and moored-up wires.

How to apply it

By brush, spray, pouring or dipping.

Pack

25 litre metal drum.
